operations.label: Create Report
operations.description:
First step of the background job mode: enqueues an Income Statement report and returns the
identifier of the report session. The computation runs in the background - poll
`.../{session_uuid}/status/` until the status is `ready`, then page through
`.../{session_uuid}/rows/`. Sessions are kept for 24 hours.

Either `period` (one column per calendar period) or `group_by` (one column per dimension
object) shapes the report; requesting both is rejected, requesting neither falls back to
`period=month`. `account_ids`, `entry_category_ids` and `work_order_ids` narrow the entries
the report aggregates.

`business_unit_ids` in the response is the effective list the report is computed for - the
requested units, or every unit the token has access to when `business_units` was omitted.


Scope: `incomestatement:report`

operations.label: Get Report Rows
operations.description:
Aggregation facts of a ready report session, paginated with `limit` and `offset`.
Answers `409` while the report is still being computed and `404` when the session expired,
never existed or belongs to another user.

One row is one register x one report column. Exactly ONE dimension column is filled and it
matches the way the session was requested: `date` in `period` mode, and `business_unit_id` /
`account_id` / `gl_category_id` / `work_order_id` / `source_id` / `industry_id` for the
matching `group_by`; the remaining dimension columns stay `null`. A dimension value of `0`
means Uncategorized - the entries carrying no reference of that model.

`debit` and `credit` are the raw turnovers of the register within the column;
`amount` is the net movement in the register's `normal_balance` direction (`credit` for
revenue/liabilities, `debit` for expenses/assets). All amounts are JSON numbers. Rows are
ordered by `register_id`. Assembling the template tree and the totals is left to the
integrator.


Scope: `incomestatement:report`

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of results to return per page.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The initial index from which to return the results.

operations.label: Get Report Status
operations.description:
Progress of a report session. This operation is exempt from the API rate limits, so it can
be polled as often as needed.

`pending` and `processing` mean the report is still being computed, `ready` means the rows
can be read, `failed` reports the error in the `error` field. A session that never existed,
expired or belongs to another user answers `404`.


Scope: `incomestatement:report`

operations.label: Get Report Feed
operations.description:
The whole report in one idempotent request, for reporting and BI tools that cannot drive
the create/status/rows flow: the report arguments travel as query-string parameters and no
session has to be remembered between calls.

The first call enqueues the background computation and answers `202 Accepted` with a
`Retry-After: 20` header and the status body. Repeating the very same `GET` attaches to
that computation (the arguments form the idempotency key, per user, for 15 minutes)
instead of starting a second one, and keeps answering `202` until the session is ready;
then it answers `200` with the same paginated rows the `.../{session_uuid}/rows/` operation
returns. A result computed for identical arguments less than 15 minutes ago is served
immediately.

List arguments accept a comma-separated value (`business_units=3,7`) or a repeated key.
An argument that is not set is left out of the URL - a query parameter is never sent as an
explicit null. An empty or null-valued key is tolerated and read as left out, so it builds
the same idempotency key.
Everything else - validation, business-unit clamping, row semantics, pagination - matches
the create and rows operations.

po_detail_uuid.description: `PurchaseDetail.detail_uuid` of the Purchase Order line this Bill line pays for. Stable across Purchase Order revisions, unlike the line `id`. Requires `purchase_order` in the same line, and the value has to name a line of the `item_uuid` of this one - an `item_uuid` of another item is refused. When `item_uuid` is omitted, an update uses the item of the matched line, and a new line takes the item of the Purchase Order line it names. An explicit `null` unlinks the line and has to come with `purchase_order: null`: a line that pays for no Purchase Order line cannot name a Purchase Order. A stored value that no longer names a line of the current revision is answered, not cleared silently.
`PurchaseDetail.detail_uuid` of the Purchase Order line this line pays for, or `null` when the line is not linked to one. Set from the `po_detail_uuid` of the save payload.
